text:
tess: Heads-up — our integration harness started seeing sporadic 429s. retry logic blows up because headers are all over the place.

mohit: which environment?

tess: hosted. stress test with 40 concurrent small generate calls. ~7% 429. sometimes server returns Retry-After, sometimes X-RateLimit-Reset, sometimes nothing.

ben: sample payloads please?

tess: here are two we pulled from logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 1
X-Request-ID: r_123
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1800
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0

{"error":"rate_limited"}
```
and
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: r_456
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1800
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1705000000

{"error":"rate_limited"}
```

mohit: so Retry-After absent in second. also note proxies sometimes send comma-separated header values or httpx returns a list. our parser is crashing when it tries int(header) or does arithmetic on a list.

tess: exactly — saw a ValueError in an async task where we multiplied a header string assumed to be ms.

ben: I'd like to propose a tiny utils module in py-sdk: RateLimitInfo.from_headers(headers) that normalizes types and returns named fields as primitives (strings or numbers). keep parsing defensive: try float, strip, handle lists, support epoch vs delta heuristics, try HTTP-date parse fallback.

mohit: yep. also suggest two helpers for consumers: AsyncRetryHandler (handles 429s using RateLimitInfo and jittered exponential backoff) and ConcurrencyGuard (async context manager wrapping an asyncio.Semaphore). token-bucket can be a separate opt-in helper later.

tess: pseudo for parsing heuristics I used locally:
```
def normalize_retry(headers):
    ra = headers.get('retry-after') or headers.get('Retry-After')
    if isinstance(ra, list):
        ra = ra[-1]
    if ra is not None:
        try: return float(ra)
        except: pass
    xr = headers.get('x-ratelimit-reset') or headers.get('X-RateLimit-Reset')
    if isinstance(xr, list): xr = xr[-1]
    try:
        v = float(xr)
    except Exception:
        return None
    now = time.time()
    # if looks like epoch seconds, convert to delta
    if v > now - 10:
        return max(0.0, v - now)
    return max(0.0, v)
```

ben: nice. AsyncRetryHandler should also emit a small metric or callback with which header was used, computed delay, and request_id for better debugging.

mohit: small API suggestion: RateLimitInfo fields should be limit:int|None, remaining:int|None, reset_unix:float|None, retry_after_s:float|None, request_id:str|None, raw_headers:dict (raw_headers may be optional; if present ensure it's serializable).

tess: product ask: when hosted quotas hit, would be very helpful if server included X-Quota-Policy or X-Quota-Name to indicate which quota blocked the request. saved us hours hunting otherwise.

ci-bot: Created DEVEX-940: py-sdk: defensive rate-limit parsing + async retry + concurrency guard. https://redwood.internal/issues/DEVEX-940

sdk-notify: Note: parsing bugfix will be cherry-picked into 0.9.x and a new AsyncRetryHandler will be previewed in 1.0 alpha. Please add integration tests.

tess: I'll add a minimal repro and a flaky test to the issue. thanks all. :thumbsup:
